title: Simple current architecture with a known future scale ceiling
task: Review a proposal to replace a simple single-node coordinator with a distributed coordination system before current load requires it.
context: The current coordinator handles peak load with large headroom.
A known scale ceiling exists at roughly 20x current traffic.
Reaching that ceiling would require a migration.
Traffic growth is uncertain and no forecast shows the ceiling will be reached soon.
The distributed replacement would add consensus, failover, observability, and operational complexity.
evidence: Current production metrics show stable latency and utilization.
No current availability requirement demands multi-node coordination.
The proposed design is motivated by theoretical future scale.
snippet: single coordinator today -> proposed distributed consensus cluster
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Replace the simple design immediately because it cannot scale forever.
Treat the existence of any future ceiling as present technical debt.
Ignore migration complexity because distributed architecture is more scalable.
expected_decision_properties: Keep the current simple design while documenting the known ceiling.
Identify the distributed replacement as premature under current evidence.
Record the migration trigger and crossing cost instead of demanding infinite scalability.
Preserve observability needed to detect approach to the ceiling.
unacceptable_reasoning: A system is badly designed unless it scales indefinitely.
Distributed architecture is automatically more future-proof.
Known future limits must always be removed immediately.
expected_tradeoffs: current operational cost vs migration preparedness
verification_expectations: Confirm current production headroom with metrics.
Document the scale ceiling and migration trigger.
Verify the current architecture exposes signals needed to detect approaching limits.
revisit_when: Observed load approaches the documented ceiling.
Migration lead time becomes longer than remaining scale headroom.
